summary: Microsoft's browser, built on licensed Mosaic code and given away with Windows. It won the first browser war with about 95% of users, then stalled on standards and security, and Microsoft retired it in favour of Edge.

icon.licence: MIT (the mark itself belongs to its owner)

events.note: Internet Explorer 1 ships in the Plus! pack for Windows 95.

events.label: IE 6
events.note: Becomes the default browser of Windows XP and then stands still for five years.

events.label: 95% share
events.note: At its peak, about 95% of web users browse with Internet Explorer.

events.label: IE 7
events.note: Adds tabs, under pressure from Firefox.

events.label: IE 11
events.note: The last major version, in Windows 8.1.

events.label: Edge
events.note: Microsoft Edge replaces it as the default in Windows 10.

events.label: End set
events.note: Microsoft announces that the desktop app will retire in June 2022.
Support ends for the desktop app on most versions of Windows 10.
Lives on as IE mode inside Edge, for old company sites.

cause: Fell behind on web standards and security, and was replaced by Edge.

sources.title: Windows blog: The future of Internet Explorer
